title: Distinguish account restrictions
goal: Separate locked passwords, account expiry and a non-login shell using observed guest behavior.
challenge: Create locked ll-u7. Inspect locked status, test past account expiry and nologin restrictions, and compare privileged explicit-identity execution. Restore only expiry/shell; keep its password locked. Do not create credentials or change PAM.

steps.command: ! getent passwd ll-u7 && ! getent group ll-u7 && test ! -e /home/ll-u7 && sudo useradd -m -U -s /bin/bash ll-u7
steps.explanation: Fail closed if this disposable name or home exists. -m creates a home from /etc/skel; -U creates a primary group; no password is set.
steps.expected: Fresh account ll-u7, same-named primary group, home and Bash shell. A nonzero status/collision means stop setup.

steps.command: sudo passwd -l ll-u7; sudo passwd -S ll-u7; sudo runuser -u ll-u7 -- id
steps.explanation: The new password was already locked. Locking is idempotent; privileged runuser still runs as that identity. No password-authentication success/failure is being tested.
steps.expected: L remains L; ll-u7 process executes. No unlocking or passwords.

steps.command: sudo chage -E 2000-01-01 ll-u7; sudo chage -l ll-u7; sudo su - ll-u7 -c id; printf "su status=%s\n" "$?"
steps.explanation: Set a past account expiry, distinct from password ageing. This guest's su PAM account check must be observed; do not generalize every privileged launcher.
steps.expected: Expired account refused by su; nonzero status. Existing processes are not killed.

steps.command: sudo runuser -u ll-u7 -- id; sudo chage -E -1 ll-u7
steps.explanation: Explicit runuser uses a different policy and still initializes the identity in this guest. Remove expiry only; password remains locked.
steps.expected: runuser succeeds despite expiry; expiry restored to never. This is not an authentication bypass granted to unprivileged users.

steps.command: sudo usermod -s /usr/sbin/nologin ll-u7; sudo su - ll-u7 -c id; sudo runuser -u ll-u7 -- id
steps.explanation: su selects the account shell, so nologin exits. A root-launched explicit command need not use that shell.
steps.expected: su emits account unavailable; runuser id succeeds.

steps.command: sudo usermod -s /bin/bash ll-u7; sudo passwd -S ll-u7; getent passwd ll-u7; sudo chage -l ll-u7
steps.explanation: Restore Bash and no account expiry but retain locked password. No sudo/remote access granted.

hints: A locked password is not a universal account/process disable switch.
Account expiry is not password expiry; each consumer's PAM policy matters.
nologin restricts shell-based entry, not arbitrary commands started by root or existing processes.
review: Retain separate status/output for locked, expired, nologin and restored states, with runuser identity evidence.
State limits: no real password login, alternative token, remote service or existing-process termination was tested.
coverage: LPIC-1 107.1 limited accounts and chage; preparation only for LPIC-2 210.2. Partial coverage; original material, self-review only. No automatic assessment or full LPIC preparation.
